articles.title: 60 Funny Book Jokes That Are Bound to Crack You Up
articles.content:
1. 为什么书要去看骨科医生？因为有人伤了它的脊椎。
2. 词典在面包店点了什么？同义词卷。
3. 什么是蛇最喜欢的文学类型？嘶嘶的历史小说。
4. 书在冬天穿什么？封套。
5. 为什么两本书成为最好的朋友？因为它们总在同一页。
6. 图书在闹腾时说什么？"用杜威小数法跟我说话。"
7. 图书对焦虑的邻居说什么？"整理好你的书架！"
8. 自信的书在借书处说什么？"尽管根据封面判断我吧。"
9. 为什么教科书在医院很紧张？它要去切除附录。
10. 为什么小说不适合保守秘密？因为它们是公开的书。
11. 为什么烹饪书被邀请参加每个派对？因为它总能调味。
12. 序言对结语说什么？"好久不见！"
13. 海盗最喜欢书的哪一部分？故事的"啊啊啊"部分。
14. 青蛙最喜欢的书是什么？有快乐结局的书。
15. 为什么番茄在小说中脸红？因为到了精彩部分。
16. 调皮的书在图书馆对男孩子说什么？"借我一看。"
17. 什么是夸耀的书？自封的书！
18. 图书馆员最喜欢的晚餐是什么？"寂静烤肉串！"
19. 小偷为什么不抢图书馆？他知道他们会严惩他。
20. 图书馆员为什么带梯子上班？为了接触更高的教育区。
21. 为什么鬼魂在图书馆游荡？因为听说那里有最好的"呜呜"书。
22. 为什么骷髅要图书馆卡？他想增强读书能力。
23. 图书馆员返还书籍时说什么？"归还的书，甜蜜的书。"
24. 图书馆最安静的宠物是什么？"哈士奇宝宝。"
25. 吸血鬼在图书馆首先去哪个区？最佳流通区。
26. 为什么巫师喜欢图书馆？每个书架都有魔法读物。
27. 为什么图书馆员拒绝邀请？她的日程已经排满。
28. 图书馆装修时招牌上写什么？"原谅我们的封套！"
29. 书对书架说什么？"谢谢你的支持！"
30. 图书馆员对闺蜜在女孩之夜说什么？"散文优先于兄弟！"
31. 为什么图书馆的猫升职了？它擅长抓书虫。
32. 为什么图书馆不举办摇滚音乐会？书已经有很多音量。
33. 为什么亚哈船长无法放松？他总是有鲸鱼的问题。
34. 《白鲸》最喜欢的晚餐是什么？鱼和船。
35. 书虫的气球在风中发生了什么？一个飘过疯人院。
36. 为什么奥德修斯欠了历史上最大的逾期费？他的图书馆书超期20年。
37. 达西先生最喜欢的运动是什么？吞下骄傲。
38. 盖茨比最喜欢的花是什么？菊花，老伙计。
39. 小精灵最喜欢的书是什么？《香蕉卡伦尼娜》。
40. 多西在奥兹建立书友会为什么？证明没有比书更好的地方！
41. 老人与海为什么不放弃他的书？他沉迷于结局。
42. 为什么杰基尔博士携带两张图书馆卡？海德先生总是积欠罚款。
43. 批评家对《双城记》说什么？这是最好的读物，也是最差的读物。
44. 鬼魂猎人的最爱俄国小说是什么？《污点与惩罚》。
45. 《1984》最喜欢的歌手是谁？乔治·奥威尔男孩。
46. 恐怖爱好者最喜欢的甲壳类动物是什么？斯蒂芬·金大闸蟹。
47. 亚历山大·杜马最喜欢的巧克力棒是什么？银河。你可能以为我会说《三枪手》，但他讨厌《三枪手》！
48. 读者在篝火旁点了什么？更多章节！
49. 为什么书虫感觉不舒服？某些读物消化不良。
50. 速读者如何赢得比赛？她总是跳到前面。
51. 为什么待读书单像洗衣服？每次看过去都会增长。
52. 书虫最喜欢的菜肴是什么？文本墨西哥菜。
53. 为什么书店雇用咖啡师？让客户表达对阅读的热爱。
54. 读者的健身是什么？缺少书架空间。
55. 什么书是臭鼬读的？最畅销书！
56. 什么书是奶牛读的？奶牛电影。
57. 什么书是猫头鹰读的？呼呼的推理小说。
58. 什么书是攀岩者读的？悬崖式结局的书。
59. 读者如何保持健康？他们实践"自我关怀"。
60. 茶爱好者对书爱好者说什么？"读了就泡。"
articles.summary:
Best book jokes

  • Why did the book go to the chiropractor?
    Someone cracked its spine.
  • What did the thesaurus order at the bakery?
    A synonym roll.
  • What’s a snake’s favorite genre?
    Hiss-torical fiction.
  • What do books wear in the winter?
    Dust jackets.
  • Why did the two books become best friends?
    They were always on the same page.
  • What did the library book say when it was feeling frisky?
    “Talk Dewey to me.”
  • What did the library book say to its anxious neighbor?
    “Get your shelf together!”
  • What did the confident book say at the checkout desk?
    “Go ahead—judge me by my cover.”
  • Why was the textbook nervous at the hospital?
    It was there to have its appendix removed.
  • Why do novels make terrible secret keepers?
    Because they’re open books.
  • Why did the cookbook get invited to every party?
    It really knew how to spice things up.
  • What did the prologue say to the epilogue?
    “Long time, no see!”
  • What’s a pirate’s favorite part of a book?
    The arrrr-c of the story.
  • What’s a frog’s favorite kind of book?
    Anything with a hoppy ending.
  • Why did the tomato blush in the middle of the novel?
    It got to the juicy part.
  • What did the flirty book say to the guy she met in the library?
    “Check me out.”
  • What do you call a book that brags all the time?
    Full of itshelf!

Library jokes

  • What’s a librarian’s favorite dinner?
    Shhh-kabobs!
  • Why did the burglar skip robbing the library?
    He knew they’d throw the book at him.
  • Why did the librarian bring a ladder to work?
    To reach the higher education section.
  • Why did the ghost haunt the library?
    It heard the place had the best boo-ks in town.
  • Why did the skeleton get a library card?
    He wanted to bone up on his reading.
  • What did the librarian say when the book was returned?
    “Tome sweet tome.”
  • What’s the quietest pet in the library?
    A hush puppy.
  • What section does a vampire visit first at the library?
    The one with the best circulation.
  • Why did the wizard love the library?
    Every shelf was full of spellbinding reads.
  • Why did the librarian turn down the invitation?
    Her schedule was totally booked.
  • What did the sign say during the library renovation?
    “Pardon our dust jackets!”
  • What did the library books say to the bookshelf?
    “Thanks for the support!”
  • What did the librarian say to her BFF on girls’ night?
    “Prose before bros!”
  • Why did the library cat get promoted?
    It was purr-fect at catching bookworms.
  • Why don’t libraries host rock concerts?
    The books already have plenty of volumes.

Novel jokes

    • Why couldn’t Captain Ahab ever relax?
      He always had a whale of a problem.
    • What’s Moby-Dick’s favorite dinner?
      Fish and ships.
    • What happened to the bookworm’s balloons on a windy day?
      One blew over the cuckoo’s nest.
    • Why did Odysseus owe the biggest late fee in history?
      His library book was 20 years overdue.
    • What’s Mr. Darcy’s favorite exercise?
      Swallowing his pride.
    • What’s Jay Gatsby’s favorite flower?
      A Daisy, old sport.
    • What is a Minion’s favorite book?
      Banana Karenina.
    • Why did Dorothy start a book club in Oz?
      To prove there’s no place like tome!
    • Why did the Old Man and the Sea never give up on his book?
      He was hooked on the ending.
    • Why did Dr. Jekyll carry two library cards?
      Mr. Hyde kept racking up late fees.
    • What did critics say about A Tale of Two Cities?
      It was the best of reads, it was the worst of reads.
    • What’s the Ghostbusters’ favorite Russian novel?
      Slime and Punishment.
    • What’s 1984‘s favorite singer?
      Boy George Orwell.
    • What’s a horror lover’s favorite crustacean?
      Steven King Crab.
    • What’s Alexandre Dumas’s favorite candy bar?
      Milky Way. (I bet you thought I was going to say Three Musketeers. He hates Three Musketeers!)

Reading jokes

  • What did the reader order at the campfire?
    S’more chapters!
  • Why did the bookworm feel sick?
    Something he read didn’t digest well.
  • How did the speed reader win the race?
    She always skipped ahead.
  • Why is a TBR pile like laundry?
    It multiplies every time you look away.
  • What’s a bookworm’s favorite cuisine?
    Text-Mex.
  • Why did the bookstore hire a barista?
    So customers could espresso their love of reading.
  • What’s a reader’s cardio?
    Running out of shelf space.
  • What kind of books do skunks read?
    Best-smellers!
  • What kind of books do cows read?
    Moo-vels.
  • What kind of books do owls read?
    Hoot-dunits.
  • What kind of books do mountain climbers read?
    Cliff-hangers.
  • How do readers stay healthy?
    They practice shelf-care.
  • What did the tea lover say to the book lover?
    Read it and steep.

Why trust us

Reader’s Digest has been telling jokes for more than 100 years, curated and reviewed over the last 20 years by Senior Features Editor Andy Simmons, a humor editor formerly of National Lampoon and the author of Now That’s Funny. We’ve earned prestigious ASME awards for our humor—including comical quips, pranks, puns, cartoons, one-liners, knock-knock jokes, riddles, memes, tweets and stories in laugh-out-loud magazine columns such as “Life in These United States,” “All in a Day’s Work,” “Laughter, the Best Medicine” and “Humor in Uniform,” as well as online collections such as short jokes, dad jokes and bad jokes so bad, they’re great. You can find a century of humor in our 2022 compendium, Reader’s Digest: Laughter, the Best Medicine. For this story on book jokes, Laura Beck tapped her 15-plus years of experience as a professional humor writer for TV shows and magazines. Read more about our team, our contributors and our editorial policies.

articles.title: These 7 Fast-Food Chains Actually Make Their Food from Scratch! Here’s Where to Go for Fresh Eats
articles.content:
我们每个人都有自己死忠的快餐品牌——无论别人怎么说，我们总会为它辩护。对于某些人来说，这个品牌是麦当劳。而对于我来说，则是Chick-fil-A和汉堡王（那道辣脆鸡肉汉堡简直好到不真实）。因此，当我偶然在抖音上看到一个视频，探讨哪些快餐连锁店使用新鲜食材并即时制作食品时，我不禁停下了脚步。

难道真的有快餐店会为了提供新鲜食材和现做现卖而多费一番心思，而不是依赖冷冻或预制食品？显然，确实有！听到这个消息后，我立即展开了调查，希望找到这些“传说中的”品牌……并希望对我的快餐偏好感到更舒心。

继续阅读，了解哪些快餐连锁店使用新鲜食材制作食品，以及他们如何处理一天结束时的剩余食物。你会惊讶地发现，哪些品牌提供的食品比你想象的更新鲜。

大多数快餐店依赖冷冻、预煮或预制的食材，在顾客下单后进行烹饪、加热或组装。虽然“冷冻”听起来似乎不太好，但实际上它是受到严格监管的。根据FDA的《食品法典》，冷冻食品必须保持在0华氏度或以下，不能在室温下解冻（必须安全地在冰箱中、冷水下或烹饪过程中解冻），而烹饪过的食品不能在“危险区间”（40至140华氏度）停留超过两小时，因为这个温度范围是细菌繁殖最快的。

此外，USDA要求冷冻或预煮的禽肉在上桌前必须加热至内部温度达到165华氏度。这也是为什么快餐店的厨房依赖带有内置计时器和温度控制的油炸锅、烧烤架和烤箱：它们帮助确保每一份订单都能得到一致和安全的烹饪。

即便如此，新鲜食品仍然胜过冷冻食品，这也是为什么你会对以下名单感到好奇。

在Five Guys的厨房里，等待午餐高峰之前，你会看到更多像是预置厨房的景象，而非快餐店。员工们在早晨手工切番茄、洋葱、生菜、蘑菇和辣椒，同时分装新鲜的、从未冷冻过的牛肉，这些牛肉只在顾客下单后才会烹饪。（有趣的是：Five Guys的店里甚至没有冷冻库——没有微波炉、保温灯或计时器。）

这样的准备工作相当了不起，考虑到这家连锁店已经发展到全球大约1,700家门店，其中大部分位于美国。这也是为什么你的汉堡可能需要多等几分钟。

虽然Five Guys没有公开宣布公司范围内关于未使用食材的处理政策，但许多决定都由个别加盟店主决定。不过，通过全天的准备工作，已经避免了大量的浪费。

In-N-Out的菜单非常简洁，你几乎可以在一次驱车到店的过程中记住它，这正是它的目的。将汉堡、薯条和奶昔放在菜单的中心，使得这家连锁店可以专注于新鲜度，而无需处理数十种食材。在其400多家门店中，主要位于加州和美国西部地区，餐厅每天都能获得新鲜的、从未冷冻过的牛肉，切配生菜，并在厨房里将整个土豆制成薯条。汉堡直到顾客下单时才会组装，这也解释了为什么有时候排队的人会绕着街区排队。

在你开始考虑是否要选择花椰菜乳酪汤还是三明治之前，Panera的烘焙师已经开始了辛勤的工作。面包、贝果和点心每天都新鲜烘焙。蔬菜被切配，三明治、沙拉和汤在服务期间不断准备。这一每日烘焙的例行工作在超过2,200家Panera咖啡馆中进行，使其成为全国最大的面包连锁店之一，而不仅仅是另一家三明治店。

但是，很多人不知道的是：因为面包是每天新鲜烘焙的，Panera通常不会在第二天再卖。相反，许多门店都参与了公司的“Day-End Dough-Nation”计划，将未售出的面包和烘焙品捐赠给当地的食品银行和非营利组织，尽可能多地进行捐赠。这是快餐产业中最大的食品捐赠努力之一。

Shake Shack可能只是纽约市的一个小型热狗推车，但如今它已经发展到全球近600家门店，却没有放弃现做现卖的方式。汉堡在顾客下单后才被压在烤架上，生菜每天都新鲜准备，而这家连锁店的冷冻卡士达是每天分小批次制作的，而不是以预制桶的形式送达。这种较慢且小批量的方式，是Shake Shack在比传统快餐更高的价格下，仍能拥有如此忠实粉丝的原因之一。

该公司还与当地的食品浪费和食品回收组织合作，包括412食品救援和Last Mile食品救援。

Culver's已经成为中西部地区的最爱，凭借它的ButterBurgers、威斯康星州乳酪块和冷冻卡士达，但在这里，“新鲜”这个词确实有意义。与事先制作大批量不同，卡士达是一天中分小批次制作的，而汉堡只有在顾客下单后才会烹饪，使用新鲜的、从未冷冻过的牛肉。这意味着在大约1,000家餐厅中（主要集中在中西部地区），有大量的手工制作正在进行。但正如Culver's在其网站上所说：“这并不是最容易的方式，但我们相信这是正确的方式。”

如果你曾经想过为什么Chipotle的员工总是手持刀具，这就是原因！在第一位午餐顾客走进门之前，员工们已经手工切好了洋葱、芫荽、辣椒、生菜和番茄，手工研磨了牛油果制成酱料，烧烤了鸡肉和牛肉，制作了米饭，这些米饭将在一天中不断补充。

这看起来是一种非常传统的经营餐厅的方式，尤其是考虑到Chipotle现在已经有超过4,000家门店。新鲜的准备工作也伴随着更严格的食品安全规则：许多准备好的食材有限制的保存时间，不能无限期延续使用。与本列表中的其他品牌一样，Chipotle已经扩大了通过当地合作伙伴捐赠符合条件的剩余食品的计划，包括Harvest计划和Local Harvest计划。

使得Chick-fil-A出名的鸡肉汉堡并非来自被扔进油炸锅的冷冻鸡排。员工在每家餐厅中整天手工裹面于鸡肉，而沙拉、水果杯和许多早餐食品都是每天新鲜准备的。考虑到Chick-fil-A目前在全美和加拿大运营着超过3,000家门店，这意味着每天早晨都有大量的手工制作正在进行。

这家连锁店在关门后的表现也很突出。通过其Shared Table计划，数千家参与的餐厅将合格的剩余食品——包括鸡肉、饼干、沙拉和水果——打包给当地的收容所和非营利组织，而非扔进垃圾桶。这是全国最大的餐厅食品捐赠计划之一，帮助提供数百万份餐食，同时减少食品浪费。
articles.summary:
We all have that fast-food chain—the one we’ll defend no matter what. For some people, it’s McDonald’s. For me, it’s a tie between Chick-fil-A and Burger King. (That spicy crispy chicken sandwich has no business being as good as it is.) So when I stumbled across a TikTok answering a question about which fast-food chains make their items fresh, I did a double take.

Hold on—some chains actually go the extra mile with fresh ingredients and made-to-order meals instead of relying on frozen or prepared foods? Apparently, they do! And once I heard that, I immediately launched an investigation to find these unicorns … and hopefully feel better about my fast-food faves.

Read on to find out which chains make their food from scratch, along with what they do with excess items at the end of the day. You’ll be surprised by who’s serving up fresher fare than you think.

Get Reader’s Digest’s Read Up newsletter for more food news, fun facts, humor, cleaning, travel and tech all week long.

How do most fast-food restaurants make their food?

Most fast-food restaurants rely on frozen, precooked or preprepared ingredients that are cooked, reheated or assembled when you order. And while “frozen” might sound like a bad thing, it’s actually tightly regulated. Under the FDA’s Food Code, frozen foods must be kept at 0 degrees Fahrenheit or below, can’t be thawed on the counter (they have to thaw safely in a refrigerator, under cold running water or during cooking), and cooked foods can’t linger in the so-called “danger zone”—between 40 and 140 degrees Fahrenheit—for more than two hours, where bacteria multiply the fastest.

On top of that, the USDA requires frozen or precooked poultry to be reheated to an internal temperature of 165 degrees before it’s served. That’s also why fast-food kitchens rely on calibrated fryers, grills and ovens with built-in timers and temperature controls: They help ensure every order is cooked consistently and safely.

Still, fresh generally trumps frozen, which is why you’re going to be intrigued by the list below.

Which fast-food chains make their food from scratch?

@nterdex McDonald’s you have 24 hours to respond. Not all fast food is created equal 👀 Some chains still keep it real by making their food fresh, not frozen. We’re talking hand-formed burgers, fresh-cut fries, and ingredients that actually taste like something 🔥 When food is made from scratch, you can taste the difference immediately — the flavor is richer, the texture hits better, and everything just feels more authentic. No shortcuts, no mystery ingredients… just real food done right. From juicy burgers to fresh bread and perfectly cooked sides, these spots prove fast food doesn’t have to mean low quality. If you care about flavor, freshness, and that made-to-order experience… you might want to rethink where you’re eating 🍔 @Five Guys Burgers & Fries @Panera Bread @In-N-Out Official😎 @SHAKE SHACK @Culver’s #Fas#FastFoodUpgraded#MadeFromScratcho#FoodTokFindsalFoodOnly ♬ original sound – Prod.G_Unknown

Not all fast-food kitchens are running on the same playbook. Here’s a look at the popular chains that put surprisingly old-school prep work into your meal, and what happens to the food they don’t end up serving.

Five Guys

Watching a Five Guys kitchen before the lunch rush is a little like watching a prep kitchen instead of a fast-food restaurant. Employees spend the morning hand-cutting potatoes for the chain’s famous fries. They slice the tomatoes, onions, lettuce, mushrooms and peppers, all while portioning fresh, never-frozen beef that’s cooked only after you order. (Fun fact: There aren’t even freezers in Five Guys restaurants—or microwaves, heat lamps or timers.)

That level of prep is pretty impressive considering the chain has grown to roughly 1,700 locations worldwide, with the majority of those in the U.S. It’s also why your burger might take a few extra minutes.

While Five Guys doesn’t publicly share a company-wide policy for what happens to every unused ingredient at the end of the day, many decisions are left to individual franchise owners. But the focus on prepping throughout the day avoids waste in the first place.

In-N-Out

In-N-Out’s menu is so small, you can practically memorize it in one drive-thru visit, and that’s exactly the point. Keeping burgers, fries and shakes at the center of the menu allows the chain to focus on freshness instead of juggling dozens of ingredients. Across its 400-plus locations, mostly in California and the western U.S., restaurants receive fresh, never-frozen beef, slice produce daily and turn whole potatoes into fries right in the kitchen. Burgers aren’t assembled until you order them, which helps explain why the line sometimes stretches around the block.

Panera Bread

Long before you’re debating between broccoli cheddar soup and a sandwich, Panera’s bakers have already been hard at work. Bread, bagels and pastries are baked fresh every day. Vegetables are chopped, and sandwiches, salads and soups are prepped throughout service. That daily baking routine happens across more than 2,200 Panera cafes, making it one of the country’s largest bakery chains, not just another sandwich shop.

But here’s the part most people don’t realize: Because the bread is baked fresh daily, Panera generally doesn’t sell it the following day. Instead, many locations participate in the company’s Day-End Dough-Nation program, donating unsold bread and baked goods to local food banks and nonprofits whenever possible. It’s one of the largest food donation efforts in the fast-casual industry.

Shake Shack

Shake Shack may have started as a tiny New York City hot dog cart, but today it has grown to nearly 600 locations around the world without abandoning its made-to-order approach. Burgers are smashed on the grill after you order, produce is prepped fresh daily, and the chain’s frozen custard is churned in small batches throughout the day instead of arriving as premade tubs. That slower, small-batch approach is part of why Shake Shack has developed such a loyal following despite charging a little more than traditional fast food.

The company also partners with local food-waste and food-recovery organizations, including 412 Food Rescue and Last Mile Food Rescue.

Culver’s

Culver’s has become a Midwest favorite for its ButterBurgers, Wisconsin cheese curds and, of course, frozen custard—but the word fresh actually means something here. Instead of making huge batches ahead of time, the custard is produced in small batches throughout the day, while burgers are cooked only after customers place an order using fresh, never-frozen beef. That’s a lot of made-from-scratch cooking happening across roughly 1,000 restaurants, most of them clustered throughout the Midwest. But as Culver’s puts it on their website, “It’s not the easiest way to do it, but we believe it’s the right way.”

Chipotle

If you’ve ever wondered why Chipotle employees always seem to be holding a knife, this is the reason! Before the first lunch customer even walks through the door, crews have already chopped onions, cilantro, peppers, lettuce and tomatoes by hand, mashed guacamole from whole avocados, grilled chicken and steak, and cooked rice that will keep being replenished throughout the day.

It’s a surprisingly old-school way to run a restaurant, especially considering Chipotle now has more than 4,000 locations. Fresh prep also comes with stricter food-safety rules: Many prepared ingredients have limited holding times and can’t simply be carried over indefinitely. Like some of the others on this list, Chipotle has expanded programs that donate eligible surplus food through local partners, including the Harvest Program and Local Harvest Program.

Chick-fil-A

The chicken sandwich that made Chick-fil-A famous doesn’t start as a frozen patty tossed into a fryer. Employees hand-bread chicken throughout the day inside each restaurant, while salads, fruit cups and many breakfast items are prepared fresh daily. Considering Chick-fil-A now operates more than 3,000 locations across the U.S. and Canada, that’s a pretty remarkable amount of scratch prep happening every morning.

The chain also stands out for what happens after closing. Through its Shared Table program, thousands of participating restaurants package eligible surplus food—including chicken, biscuits, salads and fruit—for local shelters and nonprofits instead of sending it to the trash. It’s one of the largest restaurant food donation programs in the country, helping provide millions of meals while cutting down on food waste.
